- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/28 (Sun) 17:29
- [FACT] User is considering adopting a child in the future.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Adoption can be a life-changing experience.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Typical steps involved in the adoption process include: Research and Preparation (1-3 months), Home Study (3-6 months), Application and Dossier Preparation (1-3 months), Matching and Placement (varies), Post-Placement and Legal Finalization (3-12 months).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Average timeframe for Domestic Adoption: 6-18 months; International Adoption: 12-36 months; Foster Care Adoption: 6-12 months; Private Adoption: 1-6 months.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional factors to consider in adoption include age and health of the child, agency or attorney fees (ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 or more), travel requirements, and emotional preparation.

- [FACT] User has a cousin named Alex and his wife Sarah, who adopted a baby girl named Lily from China last year.
- [EVENT] Alex and Sarah had a celebration at their church on January 15th to introduce Lily to the community.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Domestic adoption includes Private Domestic Adoption, Agency-Assisted Domestic Adoption, and Foster Care Adoption.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] International adoption involves adopting a child from another country and can be categorized into Hague Convention Adoptions and Non-Hague Convention Adoptions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Key differences between Domestic and International Adoption include child's age, waiting time, travel requirements, cultural and language differences, and cost.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Typical costs associated with Domestic Adoption range from $18,000 to $56,000, while International Adoption costs range from $31,500 to $80,000.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ways to make adoption more affordable include adoption grants, tax credits, employer benefits, fundraising, adoption loans, sliding fee scales, government subsidies, and considering agencies with lower fees.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common misconceptions about adoption include: Adoption is only for infertile couples; adopted children are not "real" family members; adoption is expensive and only for the wealthy; adopted children will have identity issues or feel abandoned; and adoption is a last resort.
